comparator.name: American Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page establishes one coherent 180-EC American Studies pathway: 60 EC of first-year courses, 60 EC of second-year courses, and a third year comprising a 30-EC minor or study-abroad semester, 10 EC in Mobility, Migration, Transculturation, a 10-EC BA thesis and a 10-EC IMPACT course. The page presents one integrated programme rather than formal routes, so no route is selected. The genuine 30-EC minor or study-abroad space remains open rather than being populated with invented content.

questions: How has American history shaped present identities, inequalities and social conflicts?

How do migration, capitalism, globalisation and regional difference connect the Americas to the wider world?

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two feasible generator-backed directions: American literature, media and cultural expression; and American politics, identity and global affairs. Each has a different organising logic, produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached. The separately assessed hemispheric migration and political-economy direction is not feasible as a 24-course Americas-focused programme because UCR lacks a sufficient regional sequence in Canada, Latin America and religion in the Americas; general global, economic and migration courses would not reproduce that target-specific direction.

alternatives.label: American society, politics & culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines American and modern history, political institutions and international relations with sociology, economics, literature, media, art, rhetoric and interdisciplinary research; the label therefore names its broad social, political and cultural composition.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible response combines American and modern history, comparative politics, international relations, sociology, economics, literature, media, art and rhetoric with qualitative, historical and documentary research.
progression: Historical, political, economic, rhetorical, literary, sociological and media foundations precede advanced work in Native American history, race and media, contemporary social theory, persuasion, documentary and historical research. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

alternatives.label: American literature, media & cultural expression
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around literary interpretation, American and global media, cultural history, visual art, race, rhetoric and creative production, so the label names the three dominant strands.
alternatives.concept: A humanities-led American Studies direction organised around literature, film, media, art, popular culture, identity and creative expression, supported by American and modern history, sociology, rhetoric and interpretive research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes economics, comparative politics, international relations, peace and conflict, Native American history and general historical research. It adds media archaeology, environmental media, documentary, film-and-text study, literary theory, creative communication and advanced art-historical methods. Nine of the 24 courses differ, shifting the organising logic from a broad society-politics-culture balance to cultural interpretation and production.
progression: Introductory literature, film and media, rhetoric, modern history, art history, sociology and research methods precede advanced literary theory, film adaptation, documentary, race and media, creative communication, persuasion and art-historical research. Every course is offered in its assigned term; no selected course has an unmet formal prerequisite.

alternatives.label: American politics, identity & global affairs
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates political institutions and ideas, constitutional and international law, history, social movements, conflict, identity, race and the United States in global affairs.
alternatives.concept: A social-science and history direction centred on American political institutions, political ideas, constitutionalism, rights, identity and social conflict, with international relations, law, empire, Indigenous history, social movements and media connecting the United States to global affairs.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route removes economics and most literature, art and general media foundations and adds law, constitutionalism, rights, empire, social movements and youth radicalisation. Compared with the culture route, fourteen courses differ. The organising emphasis is political institutions, identity, conflict and the United States in international order.
progression: Modern history, comparative politics and Law, Society & Justice precede constitutional and international law; historical, political, sociological and research foundations precede advanced Native American history, race and media, social theory, conflict, social movements and historical research. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

blocks: Modern History supplies the wider political, economic and ideological setting for the programme's second Americas survey, but is not dedicated to the Americas.
Both study modern United States history and the historical formation of social identities; UCR concentrates gender, slavery and lived experience within the broader American-century frame.
Native American Histories directly addresses Indigenous experience, settler colonialism and cultural survival, central parts of the comparator's early-Americas course.

History Research Seminar develops a substantial independent research paper through source criticism, question formulation and scholarly writing; it parallels the thesis process without reproducing a dedicated American Studies thesis.
Both examine democratic institutions, parties, political participation and challenges to democracy; UCR uses a comparative rather than exclusively American frame.
Social Movements & Environmental Justice develops social-movement theory through feminist, anti-colonial and environmental-justice cases, overlapping the comparator's New Left focus.

Introduction to Economics supplies core analysis of markets, firms, consumer behaviour and macroeconomic change relevant to capitalism, while the comparator applies these questions specifically to Latin America and the environment.
The current official curriculum leaves this rotating special-topic title unspecified, so no substantive UCR match can be asserted.
Contemporary Social Theory provides advanced concepts for analysing civil society, solidarity, trust and social change, overlapping the comparator's second cultural-theory course.
Media & Race directly examines systemic racism, resistance, storytelling and cultural power, providing a substantive counterpart to the decolonial special topic.
Life & Travel Writing examines mobility, memory, place and cross-cultural self-representation, a literary counterpart to migration and transculturation.
Both analyse how narratives shape identity and social meaning; UCR offers a general literary foundation rather than the comparator's Americas-focused integrated course.
Great Literary Works develops historical and cultural interpretation of influential narratives, although it is global rather than Americas-specific.
Creative Communication Laboratory combines research-informed cultural analysis with public-facing creative production, matching the applied cross-programme function of the IMPACT choice.
Both develop research-based written and spoken argument; UCR foregrounds rhetoric, persuasion and audience-aware communication.
Style & Meaning provides close linguistic and rhetorical analysis of how texts encode ideology and power, implementing part of the comparator's cultural-theory work.
Persuasive Communication examines framing, influence, public discourse and communication ethics, contributing a focused empirical perspective on culture and identity.
Qualitative Research Methodology teaches research design, fieldwork, interpretation and reflexivity for an independent social-cultural inquiry.
The comparator preserves 30 EC of genuine minor or study-abroad choice; no particular UCR course can be treated as its equivalent.

notes.text: Groningen's American Studies programme provides a dedicated sequence in United States and hemispheric history, politics, cultural theory, literature and media, followed by specialist work and a BA thesis. UCR can build strong programmes through American-focused courses in Native American history, gender history and media and race, combined with politics, sociology, economics, literature, media, law and research. It does not reproduce the full continuous American Studies sequence or its dedicated hemispheric survey.
